solution_name: Custom stacked ensemble of the four team models
competition_track: Team custom model (not a competition submission)
architecture: P(AI) = sigmoid(mean(logit(p_member)) - threshold_logit) over: aakash_7th_place (retrained), aditya_3rd_place, yash_5th_place, daniel_bert (retrained)

members.aakash_7th_place: artifacts/seventh/, retrained on the frozen train split by train_seventh.py (tokenizer, vocabulary, and IDF fit on train; top 500,000 n-grams)
members.aditya_3rd_place: models/aditya_3rd_place/artifacts, used unchanged (already fit on the frozen train split)
members.yash_5th_place: models/yash_5th_place/artifacts, used unchanged (already fit on the frozen train split)
members.daniel_bert: artifacts/bert/ (Hugging Face, pinned below), retrained on the frozen train split by train_bert.py

combiner_selection: Candidates were each single member, an equal mean of logits, and logistic regression on logits. They were compared by GroupKFold(5)-over-source ROC-AUC on validation. mean_logit won. The threshold maximises held-out balanced accuracy. Test and unseen_test were not used for any choice.
adaptations_from_originals: 7th place: the tokenizer, vocabulary, and IDF are fit on train (the original fit them on target or test text), and the vocabulary is capped at 500,000 n-grams.
BERT: learning rate 2e-5 with 6% warmup and weight decay 0.01. The notebook default of 5e-5 collapsed to the majority class (val AUC 0.49). Also bf16, dynamic padding, and the fast tokenizer.
BERT: the best epoch was epoch 1 (val AUC 0.99978). Early stopping used patience 2.
known_limitations: On unseen_test the ensemble (AUC 0.9953) scores below three of its members (0.9993-0.9997) because the retrained BERT generalizes worse (0.9692). Validation could not detect this because every candidate scored about 0.9995 there. This is reported as-is, with no re-selection on test data. Aditya's artifacts were pickled with scikit-learn 1.7.2, and the Hopper scoring used 1.6.1 (InconsistentVersionWarning). The scores were checked against scikit-learn 1.9.1 on 300 validation essays and were identical (max diff 1e-16). Yash's adapter requires exactly scikit-learn 1.6.1 and lightgbm 4.6.0.
training_hardware: GMU Hopper: CPU node (7th place, 5 min, 19 GB) and an A100 80GB (BERT, about 25 min)
dependencies: requirements.txt plus the member packages' requirements
inference_mode: CPU or GPU (BERT member is slow on CPU)
license_and_redistribution: bert-base-uncased is Apache-2.0; BERT member published Apache-2.0 at JaCkKnite12/cs747-custom-bert. Model owner confirmed rights to publish weights trained on the team dataset.
